title: Machine learning helps prioritize a pathway for moslosooflavone wound repair in diabetic mice
summary: Consensus machine learning on public diabetic-foot-ulcer expression data helped prioritize candidate targets for moslosooflavone, including NTRK2/TrkB. Follow-up macrophage assays and topical-hydrogel experiments in diabetic mice linked improved wound closure and macrophage polarization to TrkB/PI3K-Akt signaling. The mouse study reports three animals per group in each endpoint cohort. Pharmacological inhibition supports pathway involvement, but off-target effects, an absent osmotic control and missing NTRK2 genetic tests limit mechanistic specificity. Docking does not establish direct binding, and human efficacy remains untested.
ai_technology: XGBoost; random forest; LASSO; Boruta feature selection; TargetNet
organization: Chongqing Medical University; Chongqing University; Army Medical University

evidence.tested: Four learned feature-selection approaches prioritized five genes from two merged public transcriptomic datasets. High-glucose macrophage assays, TrkB/PI3K inhibitor experiments and a diabetic-mouse wound model tested the proposed intervention. Six groups were reported with n=3 per group and separate day-7 tissue and day-14 closure endpoint cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The internally evaluated signature lacks fully external validation. The source reports no mannitol osmotic control and no NTRK2 genetic loss-of-function test; inhibitor off-target effects remain possible. Human benefit and direct biochemical target binding are not established by these assays or docking simulations.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost, random forest, LASSO and Boruta selected consensus DFU-associated genes, intersected with predicted compound targets to prioritize CYP1A1, MAOB and NTRK2 for subsequent pathway and functional experiments.

source_review.scope: Independently read complete source-provenanced publisher text, including Methods, Results, limitations and affiliation/publication sections. Supplement files and underlying data were not independently reanalyzed.
